answer: An agent market for zephyr forecasts, jade valuations, and relic appraisals can weight voting power by escrowed stake rather than account count. Each agent locks funds for 30 days, and splitting one deposit among a thousand identities leaves its total voting power unchanged. To gain more influence, an attacker must lock more capital, sacrificing liquidity and interest; signing conflicting votes for the same decision triggers verifiable slashing of that stake.
